title: Local multi-tenant stack, generated wrangler config, tenant migration runner
goal: Generate the real deploy configuration from the agency list, run database migrations for the master and every agency, and run a local stack with several agency databases.
why: wrangler.toml [env.production] has only a name (Wrangler does not inherit bindings), ids are placeholders, MASTER_DB migrations_dir points at drizzle/tenant so master migrations are applied only by hand in seed-local.mjs, three queues used in code are unbound, and there is no way to roll a migration across agency databases.
steps: backend/wrangler.base.toml: today's wrangler.toml content without [[d1_databases]] and without [env.*]; add producer bindings AI_EXTRACTION_QUEUE (travelcrm-ai-extraction-queue, consumer with max_retries 3 and dead_letter_queue travelcrm-ai-extraction-dlq) and AI_EXTRACTION_DLQ, TENANT_JOBS_QUEUE (travelcrm-tenant-jobs, consumer max_batch_size 5, max_retries 3, dlq travelcrm-tenant-jobs-dlq; R105 writes the consumer code), [observability] enabled = true, and a comment that ids are filled by gen-wrangler from env vars CF_D1_MASTER_ID, CF_KV_CACHE_ID, CF_KV_SESSIONS_ID, CF_KV_REPORT_CACHE_ID.

backend/scripts/gen-wrangler.mjs: `node scripts/gen-wrangler.mjs --env <local|dev|staging|production> [--registry <json>] [--pool N] [--single]`. Writes backend/.wrangler.<env>.toml (gitignored): base content, MASTER_DB with migrations_dir = "drizzle/master", one [[d1_databases]] per registry entry { binding, database_name, database_id } (local: TENANT_DB_POOL_1..N with database_name travelcrm-tenant-pool-N and database_id = deterministic local UUID), [vars] ENVIRONMENT, TENANCY_MODE (single when --single, else multi), APP_URL, API_URL, CORS_ORIGINS, EMAIL_FROM (read from process.env with local defaults), and for non-local envs a complete [env.<name>] section repeating every binding (not just name). For --env local it also writes .wrangler.local-tenantschema.toml whose MASTER_DB has migrations_dir = "drizzle/tenant" and migrations_table = "d1_migrations_tenant" (single mode: both schemas in one DB, tracked in different tables because both folders start at 0000_initial.sql). Registry JSON shape: [{ tenantId, binding, databaseName, databaseId, status }].

Production registry source: `--registry <file>` (exported JSON); add `--from-d1-remote` that runs `npx wrangler d1 execute travelcrm-master --remote --json --command "SELECT id, db_binding, d1_database_id, status FROM tenants WHERE db_binding IS NOT NULL"` (not run in this batch; dry-run prints the command).
backend/scripts/fixtures/registry.sample.json: three fake tenants with fake database ids, used by the dry-run gate.

backend/scripts/bundle-tenant-migrations.mjs: reads drizzle/tenant/*.sql in name order, splits statements with readD1Migrations from @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers/config (already a dev dependency; drop comment-only statements like vitest.config.ts stripEmptyQueries does), writes src/db/tenant-migrations.generated.ts exporting TENANT_MIGRATIONS: { name: string; queries: string[] }[]. Add npm script `db:bundle-tenant` and run it.

backend/scripts/migrate-tenants.mjs: `--local | --remote --env <env>`, `--dry-run`, `--canary <tenantId>`. Order: master (wrangler d1 migrations apply travelcrm-master -c .wrangler.<env>.toml), then the canary tenant DB, then the rest in groups of 10; stop at the first failure and print which tenants are done. Local mode applies to each TENANT_DB_POOL_n by database_name.

backend/scripts/predeploy-guard.mjs + package.json: scripts deploy/deploy:staging/deploy:production become `node scripts/predeploy-guard.mjs <env> && wrangler deploy -c .wrangler.<env>.toml --env <env>`; the guard fails when the generated file is missing or older than wrangler.base.toml or still contains placeholder ids a0000000-. Add `gen:wrangler`, `migrate:tenants` scripts. db:migrate becomes `node scripts/migrate-tenants.mjs --local`.

backend/wrangler.toml stays as the developer config for plain `wrangler dev` (single mode): set [vars] ENVIRONMENT = "development", TENANCY_MODE = "single"; MASTER_DB migrations_dir = "drizzle/master"; delete the [env.dev|staging|production] stubs (deploys use generated files); keep [ai].

backend/scripts/seed-local.mjs: stop applying master SQL by hand (migrations do it now); accept `--multi` to register the demo tenant with db_binding TENANT_DB_POOL_1 and insert the demo admin user into that pool DB (wrangler d1 execute travelcrm-tenant-pool-1 --local -c .wrangler.local.toml); single mode keeps today's behaviour (admin@demo.com / Admin@123, tenant 01960000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001).

desktop/scripts/fix-stack.mjs: new flags `--multi` and `--pool N` (default 4). Replace writeE2eWranglerConfig with a call to `node scripts/gen-wrangler.mjs --env local [--pool N] [--single]` then strip [ai] from the generated file as today (keep --ai behaviour). DB setup: single mode applies master migrations then tenant migrations to MASTER_DB with the tenantschema config; multi mode applies master to MASTER_DB and tenant migrations to each pool DB; then seed-local.mjs [--multi]. Pass `--var TENANCY_MODE:single|multi` to wrangler dev. Record mode in slot<N>.json.
backend/vitest.config.ts: keep merged migrations; nothing else unless the generated file breaks it.
tests: backend/test/tenant-migrations-bundle.test.ts: TENANT_MIGRATIONS names equal the drizzle/tenant file names in order, and the count of non-empty statements matches env.TEST_MIGRATIONS tenant entries (fails when someone adds a migration without re-running db:bundle-tenant). Note: tests cannot read the file system inside workerd; compare against TEST_MIGRATIONS (names prefixed tenant_) which vitest.config.ts already passes in.

backend/scripts/gen-wrangler.selftest.mjs (Node, because workerd tests have no child_process or fs): generates production config from the sample registry and asserts 3 tenant D1 entries, an [env.production] section containing MASTER_DB, FILE_STORAGE, every queue producer, REALTIME and [vars] TENANCY_MODE = "multi", and no a0000000- placeholder when the CF_* id env vars are set; exits non-zero on any failure.
acceptance: `node backend/scripts/gen-wrangler.mjs --env production --registry backend/scripts/fixtures/registry.sample.json` writes backend/.wrangler.production.toml and `cd backend && npx wrangler deploy --dry-run -c .wrangler.production.toml --env production --outdir .dryrun` exits 0.

`node desktop/scripts/fix-stack.mjs up --slot 1 --reset-db --multi` starts; admin@demo.com logs in; the demo tenant row has db_binding TENANT_DB_POOL_1; `fix-stack up --slot 0 --reset-db` (single) still works.
`node backend/scripts/migrate-tenants.mjs --local --dry-run` prints master, canary, then the pool DBs.
The full desktop e2e suite still passes on slot 0 single mode (run once, at the end of this batch).
gate: cd backend && npx vitest run   # pass: 0 failed files and passed >= the last merged count (1296 on 2026-10-14)

cd backend && node scripts/gen-wrangler.mjs --env production --registry scripts/fixtures/registry.sample.json && npx wrangler deploy --dry-run -c .wrangler.production.toml --env production --outdir .dryrun
node desktop/scripts/fix-stack.mjs up --slot 1 --reset-db --multi && node desktop/scripts/fix-stack.mjs status --slot 1 && node desktop/scripts/fix-stack.mjs down --slot 1
cd desktop && E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3100 E2E_API_URL=http://localhost:8787/api/v1 npx playwright test
goLiveVerify: Real resource ids in env vars; `wrangler deploy` with the generated production file; `migrate-tenants.mjs --remote` against staging with a canary.
notes: Before editing read: this batch file, docs/readiness/READINESS-PLAN.md sections 0 and the design note for this area, desktop/audit/fix/FIX-PLAN.md sections 3-4 (executor rules, worktree bootstrap with node_modules junctions; never npm install inside a worktree unless the batch adds a dependency, and then only in the main checkout by the orchestrator).
Windows checkout: files may have CRLF line endings. When writing regexes over file contents (scripts, tests that read SQL or TOML), split on /\r?\n/ and never anchor on \n alone.
Both drizzle/master and drizzle/tenant start at 0000_initial.sql: never apply both to one DB with the same migrations_table.
fix-stack must keep working in existing worktrees: the generated config files live in backend/ and are gitignored.
The full e2e run in the gate is the expensive part (about an hour); run it once at the end, not per edit.
wrangler deploy --dry-run needs no Cloudflare login; if it asks for one, set CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID to a dummy value and report it.
